problem: Task specification via rewards or demonstrations is costly, and a single language instruction is often ambiguous or under-specified, so agents cannot infer how to perform the task. Prior instruction-following work is non-interactive and cannot use iterative language feedback.
motivation: Humans communicate goals with language and refine them through corrections. An agent that can ground corrections in its own past behavior could learn new tasks in a handful of trials, far fewer than RL needs and without reward engineering or demonstrations.
key_idea: Meta-train (with DAgger from per-task RL experts) a policy that ingests the instruction, its previous trajectories and the language corrections given to them, so that at test time it adapts to a new task purely through iterative language corrections.
insight: Corrections carry much more information than scalar rewards: GPR, the same model fed the trajectory reward instead of language, performs poorly on multi-room. Ablations on multi-room show that conditioning on the full correction history matters most: with only the immediate correction, completion drops to 0.63 at 5 corrections vs 0.82, because the agent forgets and undoes earlier progress. The instruction matters least (0.79 without it), since corrections can re-supply its content. Interactive corrections can beat a non-interactive full-information oracle.
method: Instruction module: word embeddings passed through a 1D CNN give the instruction embedding z_im.
Correction module: each previous trajectory (subsampled) and its correction are encoded by 1D CNNs, concatenated and passed through an MLP, then averaged over all previous trials to give z_cm.
Policy module: an MLP takes the current state, z_im and z_cm and outputs an action distribution.

Meta-training with DAgger: roll out the current policy with corrections on each training task, label visited states with the near-optimal PPO expert's actions, train by maximum likelihood, and repeat until convergence.
Correction function: a computational proxy generates corrections, either the first failed subgoal (multi-room) or directional/relational/block-identity phrases (relocation).
Meta-testing: given a new task's instruction, roll out, get a correction, and condition the next attempt on all past trajectories and corrections, for up to 5 corrections (extrapolated to 10).

setting.backbone: Small custom CNN+MLP policy with a 1D-CNN language encoder (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 1700 multi-room environments (about 51,000 corrections) and 750 object-relocation environments (33,750 corrections), with templated synthetic language from a hand-designed grammar and PPO experts
setting.observation: Multi-room: egocentric 7x7x4 symbolic grid. Relocation: 19-dim state vector of gripper and block positions. Plus language instruction and corrections.
setting.action_space: Discrete: 6 actions in multi-room (move, pickup, drop); 4 directional forces in relocation
setting.simulator: MiniGrid-based multi-room gridworld and a MuJoCo block-pushing environment
setting.privileged: Meta-train: PPO expert policies with ground-truth rewards and a programmatic correction function. Meta-test: the programmatic correction function has access to ground-truth subgoals/goal locations.

numbers.extra: 5 random seeds; completion rate = fraction of the 5 subgoals completed; unseen subgoal lists; instruction-only baseline 0.075, full-info baseline 0.73
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Mean completion rates on test tasks (Multi-room row)

numbers.extra: 5 random seeds; completion rate = 1 - final/initial block distance; instruction-only 0.64, full-info oracle 0.96

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmarks; results are on two custom simulated environments. The sample-complexity comparison with RL, pretraining+finetune and GPR is given only in a figure.
results: With 5 language corrections, completion on multi-room reaches 0.82, above the 0.73 full-information baseline (matched at 3 corrections) and far above instruction-only at 0.075. In object relocation it reaches 0.90 vs 0.64 instruction-only, approaching the 0.96 oracle. LGPL reaches high completion in at most 5 test trajectories, while the RL baseline needs more than 1000 trajectories.
limitations: Uses synthetic templated language and programmatic corrections rather than real human feedback
Only simple simulated domains; new concepts unseen in training are not handled, and it needs per-task RL experts for meta-training
Diminishing returns with more corrections, and failures when the agent forgets progress or ignores a correction
